findings.title: Storage account allows public blob access
findings.description: allow_blob_public_access exposes blob data to anonymous requests. It should be disabled unless public content delivery is intended.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage account without blob versioning
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without versioning_enabled loses protection against accidental overwrite or deletion. Enable versioning.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time restore / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: Storage account without blob soft delete
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without delete_retention_policy cannot recover accidentally deleted blobs. Enable soft delete.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account allows shared key access
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with shared_access_key_enabled = true permits storage account key authentication. Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and disable shared key access.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without infrastructure encryption
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without infrastructure_encryption_enabled lacks double encryption at the infrastructure layer. Enable it for defense in depth.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For storage accounts set `infrastructure_encryption_enabled = true` and use a customer-managed key via `azurerm_key_vault_key`. For regulated data use a customer-managed key in Key Vault with purge protection and key rotation.

findings.title: Storage account without customer-managed key
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without customer_managed_key block uses Microsoft-managed keys. Use a customer-managed key in Key Vault for sensitive data.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account queue without logging
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account queue_properties without logging loses audit trail for queue operations. Enable queue logging.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on Azure Monitor diagnostic settings, the Activity Log, and Defender for Cloud. Ship logs to a Log Analytics workspace in a security subscription.

findings.title: MSSQL server without security alert policy
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server without security_alert_policy misses advanced threat detection. Enable security alerts.
findings.remediation:
Enable the security alert policy and clear disabled_alerts so all
threat types are detected:
resource "azurerm_mssql_server_security_alert_policy" "pol" {
  resource_group_name  = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  server_name          = azurerm_mssql_server.db.name
  state                = "Enabled"
  disabled_alerts      = []
  email_account_admins = true
}

findings.title: MSSQL server without auditing enabled
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server with no azurerm_mssql_server_extended_auditing_policy referencing it loses the database activity audit trail. Attach an extended auditing policy with a storage endpoint. The legacy azurerm_sql_server type is covered the same way via its inline extended_auditing_policy block (it has no standalone policy resource).
findings.remediation:
Attach an extended auditing policy to the server:
resource "azurerm_mssql_server_extended_auditing_policy" "audit" {
  server_id                  = azurerm_mssql_server.db.id
  storage_endpoint           = azurerm_storage_account.audit.primary_blob_endpoint
  storage_account_access_key = azurerm_storage_account.audit.primary_access_key
  retention_in_days          = 90
}

findings.title: MSSQL auditing retention less than 90 days
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server_extended_auditing_policy with retention_in_days < 90 discards audit logs too early for investigation. Retain at least 90 days.

findings.title: MSSQL server not using TLS 1.2
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server with minimum_tls_version absent or below "1.2" permits older, weaker protocol versions in transit. Set minimum_tls_version = "1.2".

findings.title: MSSQL server allows public network access
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server with public_network_access_enabled true or absent (provider default is true) exposes the database endpoint. Set public_network_access_enabled = false and use private endpoints.

findings.title: MSSQL server without Azure AD authentication
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server with no azurerm_mssql_server_azuread_administrator referencing it relies solely on SQL authentication. Configure an Azure AD administrator for centralized identity.
findings.remediation:
Add an Azure AD administrator to the server:
resource "azurerm_mssql_server_azuread_administrator" "ad" {
  server_id                   = azurerm_mssql_server.db.id
  login_username              = "sql-admin"
  object_id                   = data.azuread_user.admin.object_id
  tenant_id                   = data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
  azuread_authentication_only = true
}

findings.title: MSSQL server without private endpoint
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server with no azurerm_private_endpoint whose private_service_connection targets it keeps database traffic off the private network. Add a private endpoint with subresource "sqlServer".

findings.title: Storage account allows public nested item access
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with allow_blob_public_access = true (the provider default) or allow_nested_items_to_be_public = true exposes blob data to anonymous requests. Disable public access unless public content delivery is intended.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage blobs allow public access
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with allow_blob_public_access = true (the provider default) exposes blob data to anonymous requests. Set allow_blob_public_access = false.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage account without private endpoint
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with no azurerm_private_endpoint targeting it is reachable over the public endpoint. Connect it via a private endpoint on the storage subresource (blob, dfs, queue, table, or file).
findings.evidence: private_endpoint = no azurerm_private_endpoint targets this account
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without SAS expiry policy
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without a sas_policy block issues shared access signatures with no enforced expiry. Set sas_policy { expiration_period and expiration_action } to bound SAS lifetimes.

findings.title: Storage account allows cross-tenant replication
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without allow_cross_tenant_replication = false permits object replication to storage accounts in other Microsoft Entra tenants, enabling data exfiltration paths. Disable cross-tenant replication.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without blob change feed
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without change_feed_enabled = true records no ordered log of blob create/update/delete events, blinding incident response to data tampering. Enable the blob change feed.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account with public network access (default)
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without public_network_access_enabled = false exposes the storage endpoint to the internet by default. Disable public network access and use private endpoints instead. (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-006, which covers an explicit true value.)
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage account without network rules
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without a network_rules block accepts storage traffic from any network by default. Add network_rules with default_action = "Deny" and explicit allow rules. (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-021, which covers an explicit Allow default action.)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: SQL server without managed identity
findings.description: azurerm_mssql_server without an identity block cannot use customer-managed keys for transparent data encryption or Entra ID authentication cleanly. Enable a system-assigned identity.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without managed identity
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without an identity block cannot use customer-managed keys stored in Key Vault. Enable a system-assigned identity when CMK encryption is required.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account with shared key access enabled
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with shared_access_key_enabled (the provider default) permits Shared Key authorization, which bypasses Entra ID and cannot be scoped. Disable it and use Entra ID with default_to_oauth_authentication.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account not defaulting to OAuth authentication
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without default_to_oauth_authentication = true lets clients fall back to Shared Key auth. Default to Entra ID OAuth for data-plane operations.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account allows nested public items
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with allow_nested_items_to_be_public (the provider default) lets containers and blobs be marked public even when account-level public access is off. Disable it to enforce private-by-default.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.
